abstract: We investigate whether late-time modifications of gravity in the teleparallel framework can impact the current tension in the Hubble constant <inline-formula><mml:math id="mm1"><mml:semantics><mml:msub><mml:mi>H</mml:mi><mml:mn>0</mml:mn></mml:msub></mml:semantics></mml:math></inline-formula>, focusing on <inline-formula><mml:math id="mm2"><mml:semantics><mml:mrow><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo>(</mml:mo><mml:mi>T</mml:mi><mml:mo>)</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:semantics></mml:math></inline-formula> cosmology as a minimal and well-controlled extension of General Relativity. We consider three representative <inline-formula><mml:math id="mm3"><mml:semantics><mml:mrow><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo>(</mml:mo><mml:mi>T</mml:mi><mml:mo>)</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:semantics></mml:math></inline-formula> parametrisations that recover the teleparallel equivalent of General Relativity at early times and deviate from it only in late epochs. The models are confronted with unanchored Pantheon+ Type Ia supernovae, DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations, compressed Planck cosmic microwave background distance priors, and redshift-space distortion data, allowing us to jointly probe the background expansion and the growth of cosmic structures. Two of the three models partially shift the inferred value of <inline-formula><mml:math id="mm4"><mml:semantics><mml:msub><mml:mi>H</mml:mi><mml:mn>0</mml:mn></mml:msub></mml:semantics></mml:math></inline-formula> towards local measurements, while the third worsens the discrepancy. This behaviour is directly linked to the effective torsional dynamics, with phantom-like regimes favouring higher <inline-formula><mml:math id="mm5"><mml:semantics><mml:msub><mml:mi>H</mml:mi><mml:mn>0</mml:mn></mml:msub></mml:semantics></mml:math></inline-formula> values and quintessence-like regimes producing the opposite effect. A global statistical comparison shows that the minimal <inline-formula><mml:math id="mm6"><mml:semantics><mml:mrow><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo>(</mml:mo><mml:mi>T</mml:mi><mml:mo>)</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:semantics></mml:math></inline-formula> extensions considered here are not favoured over ΛCDM by the combined data. Nevertheless, our results demonstrate that late-time torsional modifications can non-trivially redistribute current cosmological tensions among the background and growth sectors
title: Modified Teleparallel $f(T)$ Gravity, DESI BAO and the $H_0$ Tension
